_meta.title: Session 44 — MiniMax M3 release (1M ctx multimodal + MSA + open-weight, 2026-06-01); Biohub ESM page confirms S42 coverage
_meta.context: User-provided 2 links: (1) https://www.minimax.io/blog/minimax-m3 — TODAY release of MiniMax M3, native multimodal (image+video input), MiniMax Sparse Attention (MSA), 1M context, open-weight; (2) https://biohub.ai/esm/protein/about — Biohub ESM page, confirmed JS-rendered empty shell, all content already covered by S42 ingest (ESM Cambrian + ESMFold2 71MB PDF). Only marketing landing for ESM Cambrian announcement (biohub.org news 2026-05-27) restating S42 paper SOTAs qualitatively + binder hit-rate ranges 36-88% / 15-29%. NO NET-NEW DATA from Biohub side. MiniMax M3 introduces 1 NEW model + 2 NEW agentic-coding benchmarks: PostTrainBench (autonomous 'Base→ML→eval→iterate' loop in 12hr) + KernelBench Hard (% pass at Hardest CUDA kernel difficulty, distinct from existing kernelbench_l3 speedup metric) + SWE-fficiency (existing open-source dataset M3 uses for self-eval — NEW bench id to track).
_meta.rule: STRICT-ATTRIBUTION. M3 scores from MiniMax blog text (verbatim). PostTrainBench cross-comparisons (Opus 4.7 0.42, GPT-5.5 0.39) are third-party-reported by MiniMax — admitted under same practice as S37 cross-model comparison tables, flagged in note as MiniMax-reported. KernelBench Hard 28.8% registered as new bench distinct from existing kernelbench_l3 (which tracks speedup x not percent pass). SWE-fficiency registered new because it's a distinct agentic-coding bench (different from swe_bench_verified/pro). EXCLUDED qualitative-only claims: SVG-Bench 'surpasses Opus 4.7' (no number), OmniDocBench 'above Gemini 3.1 Pro' (no number — also S43 ingested OmniDocBench NED separately for Nemotron), Claw-Eval 'highest Pass³' (no number), and the 20+ benches listed in M3 blog without M3-specific numbers. SKIPPED Biohub binder hit-rate ranges (36-88% / 15-29%) — these are per-target ranges across PD-L1/EGFR/CTLA-4/PDGFRβ/CD45 with no per-model triple structure.

models.name: MiniMax M3
models._note: MiniMax M3 — native multimodal (image+video input). MiniMax Sparse Attention (MSA) architecture, 1M context. open-weight. Per-token compute 1/20 of M2. SWE-Bench Pro 59.0% (surpasses GPT-5.5 + Gemini 3.1 Pro, approaches Opus 4.7). Technical report + weights releasing over next 10 days. Parameter count not yet disclosed.

benchmarks.name: PostTrainBench
benchmarks.description: Autonomous post-training agent eval — given 4 Base models, must autonomously complete data synthesis + training + evaluation + iteration within 12 hours across AIME2025/BFCL/GPQA Main/GSM8K/HumanEval. Score 0-1 higher=better. Introduced/used by MiniMax M3 blog.

benchmarks.name: SWE-fficiency
benchmarks.description: SWE-fficiency benchmark — agentic SWE eval (open-source dataset M3 uses for self-evaluation per MiniMax blog). Higher=better.

benchmarks.name: KernelBench (Hard split, Pass)
benchmarks.description: KernelBench Hardest difficulty split — CUDA kernel generation pass rate. Distinct from existing kernelbench_l3 (which tracks speedup x metric). Higher=better.
